screenplay.text:
THE RED KITE

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     EXT. FLAT ROOF - DAY                                    1

               A flat tin roof above a row of small brick houses. Washing
               lines snap in the wind. The sky is huge and blue.

               LERATO (10), braids tied back, grips a RED KITE almost as
               tall as she is. Its tail is a string of knotted yellow
               ribbons.

                                     LERATO
                               (to the sky)
                         Come on. Come on, wind.

               A gust tears the kite out of her hands. It climbs, swoops,
               and dives straight into the washing line.

                                     LERATO
                         No, no, no!

                                     MOKGOSI (O.S.)
                         Is that my good shirt you are
                         flying?

                                     LERATO
                         It's the wind's fault!

         2     INT. MOKGOSI'S WORKSHOP - CONTINUOUS                    2

               A cramped room under the stairs. Shelves of old radios with
               their backs off, wires spilling out like roots. One bare
               bulb.

               MOKGOSI (70s), reading glasses pushed up on his forehead,
               solders a wire with a hot iron. A thin ribbon of smoke
               rises.

               Lerato bursts in with the kite under her arm. One yellow
               ribbon has torn loose.

                                     LERATO
                         Grandpa, the string is too short.
                         It only goes as high as the
                         washing.

                                     MOKGOSI
                               (not looking up)
                         Then the washing is winning. A kite
                         is only as brave as its string, my
                         girl. Short string, small sky. Long
                         string, big sky.










                                                                       2.


               He sets the iron in its stand, opens a drawer and lifts out
               a SPOOL OF BLUE STRING, fat as a loaf of bread.

                                     MOKGOSI
                         Your grandmother bought this for a
                         kite she never finished.

                                     LERATO
                         Can I have all of it?

                                     MOKGOSI
                         All of it. But listen to me.

               On the shelf, a radio crackles to life.

                                     RADIO ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
                         Strong winds this afternoon, with a
                         storm moving in from the west
                         before dark.

                                     MOKGOSI
                         You hear that? When the sky goes
                         grey, you bring it down.

                                     LERATO
                         I promise.

         3     EXT. FLAT ROOF - LATER                                  3

               The red kite is high now, a bright speck against clouds
               turning the colour of ash. The blue string hums in the wind.

               Lerato leans back against the pull, grinning.

                                     LERATO
                         Grandpa! Look how high it is! It's
                         higher than the church tower and
                         higher than the pigeons. I think it
                         can see the whole city from up
                         there, every roof, every street,
                         even our washing line. Maybe it can
                         see Grandma's old house. Maybe it
                         can see the sea!

               Thunder rolls across the roofs. The string goes tight, then
               tighter.

               SNAP.

               The kite drifts away over the houses, trailing its yellow
               ribbons, and is gone.

               Lerato stares at the empty spool in her hands.









                                                                       3.


         4     EXT. NARROW STREET - NIGHT                              4

               The storm has come and gone. The tar shines under the
               streetlights. Lerato walks alone with a TORCH, its beam
               sweeping over walls and gutters.

               At the corner, the red kite hangs from a STREETLIGHT, torn
               and dripping, its yellow ribbons stirring in the last of the
               wind.

                                     LERATO
                               (whispering)
                         There you are.

                                     MOKGOSI (O.S.)
                         Lerato! Lerato, where are you?

                                     LERATO
                         Here! Grandpa, I found it!

               Mokgosi hurries around the corner under a black umbrella,
               his slippers soaked through. He looks up at the kite, then
               down at her.

                                     MOKGOSI
                         You promised me.

                                     LERATO
                         I know. I forgot to look at the
                         sky. I was only looking at the
                         kite.

               Mokgosi hooks the handle of the umbrella over the kite's
               tail and gently pulls it free.

         5     INT. MOKGOSI'S WORKSHOP - NIGHT                         5

               The bare bulb is on. The red kite lies across the workbench,
               its torn paper patched with a page from an old newspaper.

               Mokgosi ties the last knot in the blue string. Lerato,
               wrapped in a towel, paints her name on the patch with a
               small brush.

                                     MOKGOSI
                         Tomorrow we fly it together. Your
                         grandmother used to say the sky
                         tells you everything, if you
                         remember to look up. She was right
                         about most things.

                                     LERATO
                         And we watch the sky, Grandpa.
                                     (MORE)








                                                                       4.


                                     LERATO (CONT'D)
                         Every single minute. I won't even
                         blink. Not once. Not even when the
                         pigeons come.

                                     MOKGOSI
                               (smiling)
                         And we watch the sky.

               He switches off the soldering iron. On the shelf, the radio
               plays soft music.

                                                            FADE OUT.
